title: Lisa Su, Jun Young-hyun deepen AMD–Samsung partnership across AI and foundry
key_facts: Lisa Su, chief executive and chair of AMD, held a dinner meeting on 7 Oct 2026 with Jun Young-hyun, vice chair and head of Samsung Electronics' Device Solutions division, at Samsung's Seocho office in Seoul.
The meeting lasted a little over three hours, including dinner.
Su said: 'Samsung Electronics is an excellent partner, and we always have good strategic discussions.'
Asked about foundry (contract chip manufacturing) progress, Su gave no specifics: 'Overall, we have a very broad partnership.'
Asked about physical AI (robots), Su said 'We will work together in a very wide range of areas going forward.'
In March 2026, AMD and Samsung signed an MOU on supplying HBM4 and server DDR5 DRAM and agreed to discuss producing AMD's next-generation products at Samsung's foundry.
Chosun Biz reports an industry interpretation that AMD needs more HBM supply while Samsung wants more foundry orders.
quote_evidence: "Samsung Electronics is an excellent partner, and we always have good strategic discussions."
Overall, we have a very broad partnership.

In the industry, there is an interpretation that the meeting was intended to bridge differences between AMD, which needs to expand its HBM supply, and Samsung Electronics, which is seeking to increase foundry orders.
why_it_matters_hint: AMD and Samsung are deepening talks on memory and chip making, but no foundry deal has been announced.
notes: Follow-up: parent item 1007:C08-03 (our 7 Oct edition, Korea Herald: Su courts Korean AI chipmakers). Read in full. Single outlet, no joint statement. The supply reading is Chosun's industry interpretation and is labelled as such. Pool importance 5 kept.
